[raw subtype: leptomeningeal] B: Post-contrast 3D T1 CUBE MRI of the same patient demonstrating more conspicuous diffuse nodular leptomeningeal enhancement over the left cerebellar surface, confirming leptomeningeal carcinomatosis as a manifestation of brain metastases. in_text_mentions: s. Specifically, the vasculature appears bright on post-contrast 3D T1 FSPGR but appears dark (“black blood”) on post-contrast 3D T1 FSE. As a result of the “bright blood” appearance on post-contrast FSPGR, it can sometimes be difficult to distinguish enhancing parenchymal metastases or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis (Figure 1) from background vascular enhancement (12). On the contrary, post-contrast FSE provides inherent background vascular suppression, yielding a higher contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) of lesions, making enhancing parenchymal, and leptomeningeal metastases more conspicuous (13).

A: Real patient axial and coronal post-contrast T1 MRI of melanoma brain metastases with ependymal (leptomeningeal) metastatic enhancement along the lateral ventricles, a recognized imaging pattern of leptomeningeal metastasis from brain-metastatic disease; arrows and asterisk annotations present. B: Real patient axial and sagittal post-contrast T1 MRI showing the classical linear leptomeningeal metastatic pattern along the trigeminal nerves and cerebellar surface ('sugarcoating') in lung cancer brain metastases; arrowheads/arrows annotations present. panels.figure_caption: Brain CT and MRI findings. Non-contrast CT images show hemorrhagic space-occupying lesions in the cerebellar vermis (a) and left occipital lobe (b). Axial T1-weighted images show the corresponding lesions in the cerebellar vermis (c) and left occipital lobe (d). Axial T2-weighted images demonstrate heterogeneous signal intensity and perilesional edema in the cerebellar vermis (e) and left occipital lobe (f). Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images show heterogeneous enhancement of the cerebellar vermis lesion (g) and left occipital lesion (h). Red arrows indicate representative lesions. Preoperative brain CTA, provided in Supplementary Image 1, showed no suspicious intracranial aneurysm.
in_text_mentions: al edema, most prominently in the cerebellar vermis and left occipital lobe (approximately 18 mm × 12 mm), together with additional multifocal hemorrhagic lesions in both cerebral hemispheres and the cerebellum. Multiple chronic lacunar infarctions were also present. Preoperative brain CTA showed no suspicious intracranial aneurysm (Supplementary Image 1). This supratentorial and infratentorial distribution raised concern for hemorrhagic malignant metastases or vascular lesions, but the prior history of atrial myxoma made myxoma-related brain metastases an important alternative (Figures 2a–h).

in_text_mentions: Postoperative histopathological examination revealed paucicellular myxoid neoplasms composed of scattered spindle or stellate cells with relatively abundant cytoplasm embedded in abundant myxoid stroma, with hemorrhagic change. These histological features closely resembled those of the previously resected atrial myxoma and supported extravascular tumor proliferation within the brain parenchyma (Figure 3a).

Immunohistochemical staining showed calretinin (+), CD31 (+), GFAP (–), and desmin (–) (Figures 3b–e). Calretinin positivity supported myxoma differentiation, CD31 positivity was compatible with a vascular-associated immunophenotype, GFAP negativity argued against a primary glial neoplasm, and desmin negativity argued against smooth or skeletal muscle differentiation.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial CT from a case of sarcomatoid squamous cell carcinoma with brain metastases shows a large hyperdense falx-abutting mass with surrounding vasogenic edema. The dural/falx-based appearance initially mimicked meningioma, making this an atypical imaging presentation for metastasis. B: Coronal CT view shows the same large falx-associated hyperdense mass with surrounding edema in a patient with brain metastases. The lesion's meningioma-like appearance is atypical for metastatic disease. C: Sagittal CT view demonstrates the hyperdense falx-abutting mass with perilesional vasogenic edema in the setting of metastatic carcinoma to the brain; the imaging appearance is atypical because it suggested meningioma initially.

findings.label: Perilesional vasogenic edema
findings.evidence: subcortical roundish nodule located in the left frontal lobe, with low signal in T1WI ... surrounded by a large area of edema

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial non-contrast T1WI of a real patient showing a low-signal subcortical left frontal nodule with extensive surrounding edema, captioned as a suspicious metastatic lesion in a case report of brain metastases. B: Axial T2WI of the same patient demonstrating the metastatic nodule with concentric ring signal and extensive vasogenic edema, matching the captioned brain metastasis. C: Axial DWI of the same real patient; the captioned metastatic lesion shows no apparent diffusion restriction, a recognized (non-restricted) DWI appearance of brain metastases. The panel is part of the diagnostic characterization of the same lesion rather than a control image. D: Axial contrast-enhanced T1WI of a real patient showing a subcortical left frontal lesion with peripheral ring-like enhancement and extensive perilesional edema, captioned and described in text as an intracranial metastatic tumor.
